messages.subject: Re: about only one response categories
messages.subject_clean: about only one response categories
messages.body_plain:
Hi Song Yi,

Items with only 1 observed response have no variance, so they cannot be estimated with the package. You could try to "trick" the package by including some dummy response vector that would add variance to the item, but provide a survey weight for this response of 0, but this will ultimately lead to non-convergence if a strong Bayesian prior is not included for the item parameters as there's insufficient information provided by the data for a proper solution. HTH.

Phil

Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: A question about a simulation test with small sample size
messages.subject_clean: A question about a simulation test with small sample size
messages.body_plain:
No idea what you mean by 'bringing the RMSEA down'. This statistic using M2() is a point estimate of how poorly a model fits the data in terms of first and second moments, and is influenced by a wide variety of factors (dimensionality, item-data fit, pattern of loadings, sample size, influential cases, etc). No doubt with such a small sample size the CI for the RMSEA is extremely wide, so the point estimate itself is a poor representation of how well the model fits the data. As you noted, in a perfect world RMSEA → 0 as N → ∞, so in that sense it will always be positive in any given sample, but I don't think it makes sense to look at this statistic as a function of sample size in isolation.

Phil

messages.body_plain:
I want to estimate whether there are significant changes in the subject matter competence of Norwegian pupils across birth cohorts using a large sample of standardized tests built around an anchor design.

In attempting to answer this question using mirt, I have two questions:

1. How can I get standard errors for the estimated cohort-specific means (relative to the first cohort scale that was standardized to mean 0 and standard deviation 1)?
2. The results using only anchor pupils and anchor items gives results consistent with what I have found using other approaches, but the results using all pupils and all items gives bizarre and non-credible results. Am I doing something wrong in the function call for multiGroup in this instance?

Background and data description: Norwegian 5th and 8th grade students in Norway answer a standardized test in three different subjects every year. The tests are developed using IRT methodology, and each year a random sample of pupils (~3500 out of a total of ~60 000) have a portion of the test replaced with a set of "anchor items" used to link the tests and ensure that the scale is comparable across years. The anchor items are re-used annually (but gradually renewed over the years by replacing older items with new ones).

The data I have access to are anonymized, with a line for each pupil and a column for each question. The columns are named for the question they represent, and the question-names (a numeric code) is fixed for each item. Anchor items can thus be identified as questions posed repeatedly across multiple years, and anchor pupils can be identified as pupils answering multiple anchor questions.

Viewing the anchor items and ignoring the cohort-specific items, I set up a dataset with one column for each anchor question and one line for each anchor pupil, along with a variable for which birth cohort each child (i.e. data row) belongs to. I also create a vector (named item_type) for the items as some of them are polytomous - with binary items assigned "2PL" and polytomous items "gpcm". The first line of the data gives the test year, while the remaining columns give the scores for the individual anchor items.

As I understand the documentation, the invariances I want to impose are slopes and intercepts (since the groups are years, and the assumption of the anchoring procedure is that the item parameters of the anchor items are the same over time), but also "free_means" and "free_variance" (as both the mean and the variance of later birth cohorts could differ from the first birth cohort.

I thus specify the model as
    multi_year_irt <- multipleGroup(anchor_pupil_data[, 2:length(colnames(anchor_pupil_data))],
                                     model = 1,

Since the cohort-specific items are cohort-specific, the assumed invariance for slopes and intercepts across groups should not matter for these items: they are only observed for one cohort each. I also expected that the trends in group means (i.e., birth cohort means) would change slightly but stay more or less the same. Are there issues when using large amounts of data (a single analysis would now have about 470 000 pupils, each answering a subset of about 400 total items used in the test across all years)? (The convergence alghorithm stopped after 500 iterations - should I boost this number and see if that helps?)

Sincerely,
